name: Dst_Ji2012
description:
Catalogue from Ji et al., 2012  J. Geophys. Res., 117, A03209
https://doi.org/10.1029/2011JA016872

The start times are defined as the times when there were noticeable decrease of Dst values after the corresponding interplanetary shocks (Storm Sudden Commencements, SSC) by checking the variation of the solar wind data (velocity, density, and magnetic field). The end times are defined as the times when the Dst just recovers to above −50 nT after the minimum Dst.

Dst min values are in nT.
Abbreviations are sMC, MC preceded by a fast shock; SH, sheath field; CIR, corotating interaction region; nonMC, ICME that does not show the signature of a magnetic cloud.

description:
from https://zenodo.org/record/8319481

name: ICME_multi-catalog
description:
source : https://edatos.consorciomadrono.es/dataset.xhtml?persistentId=doi:10.21950/XGUIYX
Name: Carlos Larrodera
Institution: University of Alcalá
Email: carlos.larrodera@uah.es
ORCID: 0000-0003-4231-7690

Description of the project
The main idea of the project is to gather the information of different Interplanetary Coronal Mass Ejections (ICMEs) seen by different spacecraft to obtain a combined catalog that ranges between 0.25 to 5 AU and between 1975 and 2022.
This allows us to study statistically the different structures present in the ICMEs along with their evolution with distance and time.

Description of the dataset
We have obtained a list of around 2000 separate ICMEs detailed in this file. It should be noted that the only inherited information from the original catalogs are the dates
The file contains the following fields:

- icme_start: Date of the beginning of the ICME (*) ; this is the Start Time of the catalogue
- mo_start: Date of the beginning of the magnetic obstacle (MO) (**)
- mo_end: Date of the end of the ICME; this is the Stop Time of the catalogue
- r_heliodist: Heliocentric distance of the spacecraft that detected the ICME (units=Km)
- spacecraft: Spacecraft that detected the ICME
- theta: Longitude (HCI reference system)
- lati: Latitude (HCI reference system)
- cat_source: Original catalog from which the ICME belongs (***)
- flg_sheath: Flag for presence of sheath: (1) ICME has a sheath (0) ICME has no sheath
- v_aver_0048_sw: Upstream average solar wind speed. Time range covered: Between 0h and 48h before the ICME (units=Km/s)
- v_std_0048_sw: Upstream standard deviation solar wind speed. Time range covered: Between 0h and 48h before the ICME  (units=Km/s)
- B_aver_0048_sw: Upstream average solar wind magnetic field. Time range covered: Between 0h and 48h before the ICME  (units=nT)
- B_std_0048_sw: Upstream standard deviation solar wind magnetic field. Time range covered: Between 0h and 48h before the ICME  (units= nT)
- N_aver_0048_sw: …

description: The Jupiter Icy Moons Explorer (JUICE) is an interplanetary spacecraft that was launched on 14 April 2023 the European Space Agency (ESA). Much data of interest tothe heliospheric community was obtained during the cruise phases between planetary encounters from a magnetometer and an energetic particle and plasma spectrometer. name: GEOTAIL_PlasmaRegimes
description:
Catalog of the plasma regimes (i.e. the regions) explored by GEOTAIL during its distant tail campaign (Sep.1992 - Oct.1994).
The catalog has been generated by Christian Jacquey from the original catalog produced by Christon and Eastman (1998).

 Coded values for the plasma regimes (regions) and instrument operation modes:
   0   ::  No region (only for Region 2)
   1   ::  SW (Solar Wind)
   2   ::  MS (Magnetosheath)
   3   ::  BL (Boundary Layer)
   4   ::  PS (Plasma Sheet)
   5   ::  LB (Lobe)
   77  ::  FL (Solar Flares)
   88  ::  RF (Reduced Flows)
   99  ::  Gap
   888 ::  Saturation
   999 ::  Calibration (in fligth)
   
For a given interval, the "Region 1" is the primary region where GEOTAIL was located. However for many intervals, GEOTAIl was also flying in another secondary region by intermitence. The "Region 2" parameter references this secondary region.
For selecting the intervals when GEOTAIl was exclusively in a unique region, appkly the filter: Region 2 = 0

 Please, read and respect the rules of road of the CDPP (https://amda.irap.omp.eu/help/policy.html)
 and of the original authors of the catalog (http://sd-www.jhuapl.edu/Geotail/regime_id_references.html)

Reference papers (to be cited):
Paper 1:
Eastman, T. E., S. P. Christon, et al., Magnetospheric plasma regimes using Geotail measurements 1: Regime identification and distant tail variability, J. Geophys. Res., 103, 23,503-23,520, doi:10.1029/98JA01915, 1998.

Paper 2:
Christon, S. P. T. E. Eastman, et al., Magnetospheric plasma regimes using Geotail measurements 2: Statistics, spatial distribution, and geomagnetic dependence, J. Geophys. Res., 103, 23,521-23,542, doi:10.1029/98JA01914, 1998.

name: RB-events_v01-00_1970_2021
description:
This catalog is a subset of intervals (periods after 1970) from:

 Radiation Belts Electron Enhancement Events
 source : https://doi.org/10.57745/W4HY2S

 This dataset contains the list of radiation belts electron enhancement events identified using the ground-based index Ca with the method described in the following article:
 Bernoux, G., Nguyen, G., Sicard, A., & Maget, M. (2025). Automatic Identification of Past Radiation Belts Electron Enhancement Events Using a Ground-Based Parameter. Earth and Space Science, 12, e2024EA003945. https://doi.org/10.1029/2024EA003945

 These are radiation belts electron enhancement events events corresponding to medium-energy (0.03 ≲ E ≲ 1 MeV) electrons located at the core of the outer electron belt from 1868 to 2021 (inclusive).

The list is in a CSV table with one header, 4243 data rows and 6 columns:

    id: the event’s relative identifier
    start date: event start date and time
    end date: event end date and time
    max date: date and time of maximum Ca of the event
    max value: event’s maximum Ca value (nT)
    category: probable cause of the event, which can take six values: empty cell, “icme”, “sir”, “multiple icmes”, “multiple sirs”, “sir and icme”.

Date and times are in ISO 8601 format. We may update the list occasionally in the future, for example when new definitive values of the aa index are published.

The research leading to these results has received funding from the European Union's Horizon Europe research and innovation programme under grant agreement No 101081772 (FARBES project).
